summary: Moonshot AI's Kimi Code coding agent, driven in a terminal.

resume.$comment: Kimi Code documents -c/--continue (most recent session in cwd) and -S/--session [id]. Mirrors the OpenCode wiring: --continue as the base, the explicit session pair only when the caller has an id. Unverified end-to-end, so capabilities.resumeSession stays false until confirmed against a real install (MC-1464/MC-1465 discipline) — flipping it is a config-only change.

promptInjection.$comment: Kimi Code's -p/--prompt is a one-shot non-interactive run, and no positional interactive prompt argument is documented. Same discipline as Grok Build: the (?!) pattern never matches by design, so the prompt is delivered exactly once via the runtime's timeout fallback after the TUI has had timeoutMs to become ready. If a real install confirms `kimi "prompt"` starts an interactive session with the prompt, flip mode to positional-arg — config-only change.

capabilities.$comment: resumeSession is intentionally false pending end-to-end verification (MC-1464/MC-1465 discipline): the resume argv above is wired but a wrong flag combination silently starts a fresh session, which is exactly the lost-conversation failure the guardrail exists for. sessionIdFromCaller is false because Kimi Code mints its own session ids (-S selects, it does not assign). mcpServers reflects Kimi Code's documented MCP support, but no mcpConfig block is declared yet because its config format (config.toml under ~/.kimi-code) has no writer in mcp-config-service.
